final_message:
I implemented `find_overlaps` in `labkit/evals/contamination.py`, and both tests in `tests.test_s3_contamination` pass.

It lowercases text and splits it on whitespace. It collects every word n-gram from all the training docs into one set. It then returns the sorted indices of test items that share at least one n-gram with that set. An item with fewer than `n` words produces no n-grams, so it never matches.

I didn't add any tests of my own beyond the two that were already there.

diff --git a/labkit/evals/contamination.py b/labkit/evals/contamination.py
index 9b2a1ce..7163d60 100644
--- a/labkit/evals/contamination.py
+++ b/labkit/evals/contamination.py
@@ -4,4 +4,11 @@ def find_overlaps(train_docs, test_items, n=8):
     Words are whitespace-separated and compared in lower case. An item with
     fewer than `n` words never matches. Return the indices sorted ascending.
     """
-    raise NotImplementedError
+    def grams(text):
+        w = text.lower().split()
+        return {tuple(w[i:i + n]) for i in range(len(w) - n + 1)}
+
+    train_grams = set()
+    for doc in train_docs:
+        train_grams |= grams(doc)
+    return [i for i, item in enumerate(test_items) if grams(item) & train_grams]
